caption: The drawing features a single wooden Windsor chair placed centrally within a lightly outlined rectangular border. The chair has a rounded, hoop-style backrest made of thin vertical spindles that curve upwards to meet a semi-circular top rail. It has two curved armrests, each supported by vertical posts, and a slightly contoured, rounded seat. The chair stands on four splayed, turned legs connected by two pairs of cross-stretchers for added stability. The wood appears to be medium to dark brown, and the shading suggests a polished surface. In the upper left corner of the page, there is a smaller inset sketch of the same chair drawn in finer, light brown or sepia lines, with dimensions indicated as part of its outline. The background is plain, and the paper is an off-white or light cream color. The artist's signature, "Edward Loper," along with the date "Oct 15th" appears in the lower right corner of the main drawing.
title: Windsor Bamboo-turned Chair
